geometry.note: OpenStreetMap point (rank 11), so confidence is capped at approximate. The distance checks use a 7 % tolerance, which is what a 10-15 m placement error on a 100 m spacing amounts to; the published spacings are integers read from labels on an aerial photograph.

method: OpenStreetMap node 664910895 (man_made=telescope, name=VERITAS, ref=1, telescope:diameter=12), a single point used verbatim. The node's position is the mapper's placement of the telescope, traced from aerial imagery (source=yahoo); the tracing accuracy on a 12 m dish is taken as 15 m. T1 stands at its position after the 2009 relocation (the OSM T1-T4 distance is 172 m, not the 35 m of the old layout). Distance checks measure this node against the neighbours named in Figure 1 of Perkins and Maier 2009.
name: VERITAS telescope T1 (12 m)
notes: T1 was relocated in summer 2009 (Perkins and Maier 2009); this point is its position after the move.

summary.plain: Telescope T1 of the four-telescope VERITAS array at the basecamp of the Whipple Observatory in Arizona (a 12-metre gamma-ray telescope).
